claim: The Korea Herald reported that a July 2026 JPMorgan analysis found newer memory long-term agreements increasingly run three to five years and include pre-agreed supply volumes, pricing formulas or floors, and stronger commitments such as prepayments, collateral or financial guarantees; some also use take-or-pay provisions.
evidence: JPMorgan's July analysis noted that "newer LTAs increasingly run for three to five years and include pre-agreed supply volumes, pricing formulas or floors and stronger commitments such as prepayments, collateral or financial guarantees."; "Some also use 'take-or-pay' provisions" (Korea Herald, 12 Aug 2026)
notes: Adds the JPMorgan attribution missing from CLM-1160.

claim: In June 2009 Elpida Memory agreed to sell JPY 30 billion of securities to the government-backed Development Bank of Japan under a government scheme for companies hit by the recession.
evidence: "Elpida Memory Inc., Japan's only maker of dynamic random access memory chips, will sell securities worth 30 billion yen to the government-backed Development Bank of Japan"; part of "a government scheme aimed at providing funds to companies hit hard by Japan's worst post-war recession" (IndustryWeek, 30 Jun 2009)

metric.name: DBJ investment in Elpida
metric.population: Elpida securities sold to Development Bank of Japan

notes: Corroborates the 2009 date in CLM-1174, which SRC-0375 does not state.
